userStories.title: Executor project argument (S5b-R7) and the WORKSPACE tool route
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the tool executor resolve and authorize a validated `project` argument on every WORKSPACE project-scoped call, make REPO and PROJECT threads refuse a `project` argument, and stop the runner tool route refusing WORKSPACE jobs.

**Motivation** — The koda tools are all project-scoped: the executor takes the project from the job (`assistant-tool.executor.ts:107-110`), which for a WORKSPACE job is the home project, so sending the catalog alone would silently answer every question about the home project only; and tool parsers ignore unknown keys (`tools/ticket-tools.ts:38-41`, `asRecord`), so a `project` key in a REPO thread is silently dropped.

**Approach** — S5b-R7: the executor owns the project scope; WORKSPACE tools take a validated `project` argument checked against the creator on every call; REPO and PROJECT threads refuse it.
1d2-D3 tool scope. `AssistantTool` gains `scope?: 'project' | 'workspace'`; absent means `project`. Every existing tool stays project-scoped. (`koda_my_projects` is the only workspace-scoped tool, registered in US-003; the executor logic for scope is implemented here.)
1d2-D4 the project argument (executor, S5b-R7). The executor reads the thread kind from the call context (`ToolCallContext.kind`, absent reads as `REPO`, the column default; `PrismaAssistantToolCallRepository.findCallContext`, `prisma-assistant-tool-call.repository.ts:62-72`, selects `thread.kind` and returns it). In order, after the existing disabled-creator check and before `tool.parse`:
  1. A workspace-scoped tool in a REPO or PROJECT thread -> `invalid_input: <name> is only available in workspace threads`.
  2. An input that has its own `project` key, in a REPO or PROJECT thread, or for a workspace-scoped tool -> `invalid_input: project`.
  3. WORKSPACE thread, project-scoped tool: `project` missing, not a string, or not matching the slug pattern -> `invalid_input: project`, with no lookup.
  4. WORKSPACE thread, project-scoped tool: `ProjectAccessService.findProjectIdBySlug(project)` (deleted projects miss) then `resolveMembership(projectId, actor)`. An unknown slug, a deleted project and a project the creator is not a member of all answer the same `not_found: project` (no existence oracle). A global ADMIN reaches every project, as in the web project list and the 1d-D3 home-project rule.
  5. The input passed to `tool.parse` is a copy without the `project` key. The resolved project's id and slug become `ToolContext.projectId` / `projectSlug`, and the ability check uses the role `resolveMembership` answered there.
An input that is not an object (null, an array, a scalar) has no `project` key: steps 2 and 3 treat it as absent, and `tool.parse` judges it as today. REPO and PROJECT threads keep today's path (project from the job, then `tool.parse`, then membership) once step 2 passes; a WORKSPACE project-scoped call resolves membership before `tool.parse` on purpose (steps 4-5), because the role answered for the resolved project is what the ability check needs. Membership is resolved on every call, never cached across calls.
1d2-D5 workspace-scoped execution. A workspace-scoped tool in a WORKSPACE thread runs with no membership or ability check by the executor (it reads only what the creator can reach, by construction). Its `ToolContext.projectId` and `projectSlug` are the home project's, which the tool must not read, and `ctx.actor` is `userPrincipal(creator)` with no project role.
1d2-D6 audit. `AssistantToolCall.projectId` is the resolved project for a WORKSPACE call that reached step 5, and the job's project (the home project) for every other call, including refusals at steps 1-4.
1d2-D8 the route. `RunnerToolService.call` (`runner-tool.service.ts:44-58`) no longer refuses a WORKSPACE job (line 51 is removed and `findThreadTokenScope` leaves the service's `jobs` `Pick`); every other gate is unchanged. The kill switch is unchanged: `FLEET_THREADS_ENABLED` off answers 409 `threads.disabled` on the tool route.
Workspace failure texts: ability failure keeps today's text with the resolved slug: `forbidden: <tool> needs <action> <subject> on <slug>`.
Update existing tests: `runner-tool.service.spec.ts:178-184` ("workspace AC-8 refuses tools before registry or executor") becomes a test that a WORKSPACE job's call reaches the executor with `{ jobId, toolCallId, name, input }`; `test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts:4246-4253` becomes "workspace tool route answers a held RUNNING job": the same request with `input: { project: <seeded project slug> }` expects 200 and `isError: false`.

**Scope** — In: `ToolCallContext.kind`, `findCallContext`, `AssistantTool.scope`, executor steps 1-5 and audit projectId, route gate removal, the two spec updates. Out: `koda_my_projects`, `WorkspaceTools`, `findProjectCounts`, `AssistantModule` changes (US-003); descriptors/ASSIGN (US-001).

**Interface**
```ts
// assistant-tool-call.domain.ts
export interface ToolCallContext { /* existing fields */ kind?: ChatThreadKind }
// assistant-tool.types.ts
export interface AssistantTool { /* existing fields */ scope?: 'project' | 'workspace' }
```

userStories.title: Web /threads list, new-thread page, nav and palette
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the personal `/threads` list page and the `/threads/new` page with a home-project picker, and reach them from the sidebar's Workspace section and the command palette.

**Motivation** — WORKSPACE threads are creator-only and top-level (S5b-R12); after 1d-1 there is no web entry point for them.

**Approach** — 1d2-D10 web routes. `/threads` (list), `/threads/new`, `/threads/:id`. Nuxt static routes win over `pages/[project]`, so a project slugged `threads` is shadowed in the web, as `agents`, `admin` and `settings` already are. These pages render no breadcrumbs (the layout renders none outside a project, `layouts/default.vue:73-75`).
1d2-D11 web new page. Fields: home project (a select whose first option `Automatic` (`fleet.threads.workspace.homeAutomatic`) sends no `homeProject`; the other options are the caller's projects from `GET /projects`), title, model, effort, max cost. Models come from the runner summaries of the selected project, or of the first listed project when `Automatic` is chosen (`useFleetDispatchOptions(slug)`; runner summaries are the same for every project), filtered to online, enabled runners advertising `workspaceThreads` (`eligibleModels(runners, 'WORKSPACE')`). Native backends only (ACP is refused for WORKSPACE). With no projects listed, no runner summaries load and the model list is empty. Submit posts to `/threads` using `toCreateWorkspaceThreadBody` and navigates to `/threads/<created id>`; when the API refuses (403 `threads.homeProjectAccess`, 409 `threads.noFleetRepo`) the API message is shown in the form and there is no navigation.
1d2-D14 nav. A `My threads` link (`nav.myThreads`, `MessagesSquare` icon) in the sidebar's Workspace section (`layouts/default.vue:182-197`) after Agents, and a palette command `my-threads` (`components/CommandPalette.vue:26-30`) that navigates to `/threads` and is present with or without a project.
List page: mirror `pages/[project]/threads/index.vue`; calls `GET /threads` (via `useWorkspaceThreads`) with `status` `ACTIVE`, switches to `ARCHIVED`, renders a `new` link only when `threadsEnabled` is not false (the disabled state otherwise). `ThreadListTable` (`components/fleet/threads/ThreadListTable.vue:10-15`) gains optional `basePath?: string` for the row links (default `/<slug>/threads`), and shows the home project name where a REPO thread shows `feat/<feature>` for a WORKSPACE row; `slug` becomes optional when `basePath` is given. On `/threads` the page passes a `nameOf` that answers the signed-in user's name (every row is theirs) and `basePath` `/threads`. i18n: add `nav.myThreads`, `fleet.threads.workspace.title`, `fleet.threads.workspace.homeProject`, `fleet.threads.workspace.homeAutomatic` to both `i18n/locales/en.json` and `zh.json`.
Existing threads nav and palette specs (`tests/layouts/threads-nav.spec.ts`, `tests/components/command-palette-threads.spec.ts`) assert project entries by their own ids and paths and must keep passing unchanged.

**Scope** — In: the two pages, `ThreadListTable` props, layout link, palette command, i18n keys. Out: the detail page and `ThreadHeader` WORKSPACE label (US-006), composables and lib helpers (US-004), breadcrumbs, a Playwright journey.

**Interface**
```ts
// ThreadListTable props: slug becomes optional when basePath is given; basePath?: string is new; keep the existing nameOf prop as is
// palette command: { id: 'my-threads', ... navigates to '/threads' }
```

analysis:
Feature 1d-2 finishes umbrella row 4 (S5b-1d). 1d-1 (#292) shipped WORKSPACE threads with no koda tools. EXECUTOR ORDER (1d2-D4): after the disabled-creator check and before tool.parse: (1) workspace-scoped tool in REPO/PROJECT thread -> invalid_input: <name> is only available in workspace threads; (2) input has own `project` key in REPO/PROJECT thread or for a workspace-scoped tool -> invalid_input: project; (3) WORKSPACE + project-scoped: project missing/non-string/non-slug -> invalid_input: project with no lookup; (4) findProjectIdBySlug then resolveMembership; unknown, deleted and non-member ALL map to the same `not_found: project` (no existence oracle; map ForbiddenAppException and NotFoundAppException alike); global ADMIN reaches every project; (5) parse a COPY of the input without `project`; resolved id/slug become ToolContext.projectId/projectSlug and the ability check uses the role resolveMembership returned. Non-object input has no project key (steps 2/3 treat as absent). Membership resolved on every call, never cached (AC: removed member gets not_found on the next call with a new toolCallId). Workspace-scoped tools in WORKSPACE threads skip membership/ability checks; ctx.projectId/slug are the home project's (tool must not read them), ctx.actor = userPrincipal(creator) with no project role. Audit (1d2-D6): AssistantToolCall.projectId = resolved project for WORKSPACE calls reaching step 5, else the job's (home) project, including refusals at steps 1-4. ToolCallContext.kind absent reads as REPO.

koda_my_projects (1d2-D7): no input properties (additionalProperties false); projects = ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal(ctx.actor) ordered by slug asc, first 50; one line `<slug> open_tickets: <n> failed_jobs_7d: <n> pending_approvals: <n> /<slug>` plus project name via ctx.data on the next line; `no projects` when empty; last line `more: <n> projects not listed` when >50. Counts via findProjectCounts(projectIds, failedSince) = three groupBy reads keyed by projectId returning Map with zeros for absent projects: open tickets = Ticket deletedAt null and status in CREATED/VERIFIED/IN_PROGRESS/VERIFY_FIX; failed jobs = FleetJob state FAILED|CRASHED and finishedAt >= ctx.now - 7d; pending approvals = FleetApproval status 'pending'. Exposed via interface ProjectCountsReader + token PROJECT_COUNTS_READER declared in assistant-tool-call.domain.ts (as findCallContext was in 1b-D6). Only koda_my_projects has scope 'workspace'; all existing tools stay project-scoped (absent scope = project). apps/api/src/common/test-helpers/global-stubs.module.ts may need a stub if AssistantModule compiles with the new ProjectsModule import.
